original_question: Among families of numerical semigroups closed under gluing, determine the least family that contains all numerical semigroups of maximal embedding dimension.
target_in_paper: Section 5, unnumbered open problem after the discussion of gluing: "Which is the least family containing those semigroups with maximal embedding dimension and closed under gluing?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual wording and scope. It correctly identifies that the problem is about numerical semigroups, closure under gluing, and finding the least family containing all semigroups of maximal embedding dimension. It also stays on the Section 5 gluing problem rather than broadening to neighboring questions.
missing_details: The ambient objects should be stated explicitly: a numerical semigroup is a cofinite submonoid of ℕ containing 0.

The phrase "maximal embedding dimension" should be defined: if m(S) is the least positive element of S and e(S) is the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S, then S has maximal embedding dimension when e(S)=m(S).

The paper’s notion of gluing should be stated explicitly: if S1=⟨n1,…,nr⟩ and S2=⟨m1,…,ms⟩ are minimally generated as written, α∈S1∖{n1,…,nr}, β∈S2∖{m1,…,ms}, and gcd(α,β)=1, then the gluing is ⟨βn1,…,βnr,αm1,…,αms⟩.
"Least family" should be made explicit as minimal with respect to inclusion among all families of numerical semigroups satisfying the containment and gluing-closure conditions.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the family must contain every numerical semigroup of maximal embedding dimension.

One should avoid adding a Frobenius-variety condition, because that would turn the question into a different neighboring open problem from Section 4, not the Section 5 gluing problem your draft is targeting.
refined_question: Let a numerical semigroup mean a cofinite submonoid S⊆ℕ containing 0. For such an S, let m(S) be its multiplicity (the least positive element of S) and e(S) its embedding dimension (the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators); say that S has maximal embedding dimension if e(S)=m(S). If S1=⟨n1,…,nr⟩ and S2=⟨m1,…,ms⟩ are numerical semigroups given by their minimal systems of generators, and if α∈S1∖{n1,…,nr} and β∈S2∖{m1,…,ms} satisfy gcd(α,β)=1, their gluing is the numerical semigroup ⟨βn1,…,βnr,αm1,…,αms⟩. Determine, with respect to inclusion, the least family F of numerical semigroups such that (i) every numerical semigroup of maximal embedding dimension belongs to F, and (ii) F is closed under gluing.
justification: The draft matches the unnumbered Section 5 open problem almost verbatim: the paper asks for the least family containing the maximal-embedding-dimension semigroups and closed under gluing (Section 5, p. 22). To make that question stand alone, one must import the meanings of multiplicity and embedding dimension from Section 1 (p. 15), the paper’s definition of maximal embedding dimension from Section 4 (p. 19), and the exact gluing construction from Section 5 (p. 22). I have not reformulated it as a Frobenius-variety question, because the paper treats that as a separate neighboring problem in Section 4 (p. 19), not as an equivalent version of the Section 5 question.
